title: Find All Good Indices
statement:
You are given an integer array `nums` of length `n` (indexed from 0) and a positive integer `k`. An index `i` with `k <= i < n - k` counts as **good** when both hold:

- the `k` values directly to its left, `nums[i - k..i - 1]`, never go up from one to the next (each is at most the one before it);
- the `k` values directly to its right, `nums[i + 1..i + k]`, never go down from one to the next (each is at least the one before it).

The value `nums[i]` itself takes part in neither check. Return all good indices in increasing order, or an empty list when there are none.
notes:
## Intuition

Checking the `k` values on each side of every index directly costs O(n·k). Instead, record for every position how long the monotone run touching it is. If the non-increasing run that ends just left of `i` has length at least `k`, the left condition holds; the same idea with a non-decreasing run starting just right of `i` handles the right side.

## Approach

1. Fill `before` and `after` with 1: every single value is a run of length 1.
2. Sweep left to right: when `nums[i] <= nums[i - 1]`, the non-increasing run ending at `i` extends the one ending at `i - 1`, so `before[i] = before[i - 1] + 1`.
3. Sweep right to left: when `nums[i] <= nums[i + 1]`, the non-decreasing run starting at `i` extends the one at `i + 1`, so `after[i] = after[i + 1] + 1`.
4. For each `i` from `k` to `n - k - 1`, it is good exactly when `before[i - 1] >= k` and `after[i + 1] >= k`. Collect those indices in order.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [2, 1, 1, 1, 3, 4, 1]`, `k = 2`. The left sweep gives `before = [1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 1, 2]` and the right sweep gives `after = [1, 4, 3, 2, 2, 1, 1]`. Candidates are `i = 2, 3, 4`:

- `i = 2`: `before[1] = 2` and `after[3] = 2`, good.
- `i = 3`: `before[2] = 3` and `after[4] = 2`, good.
- `i = 4`: `before[3] = 4` but `after[5] = 1` (4 then 1 goes down), not good.

The answer is `[2, 3]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): two sweeps to build the run lengths and one pass over the candidates.
- Space: O(n) for the two run-length arrays.

## Pitfalls

- Look at `before[i - 1]` and `after[i + 1]`, not at index `i`: `nums[i]` is excluded from both checks.
- Equal neighbours keep both kinds of run going, so compare with `<=`, not `<`.
- The candidate range stops at `n - k - 1` so that `k` values exist on the right.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of `nums` |
| `before[i]` | length of the longest non-increasing run ending at `i` |
| `after[i]` | length of the longest non-decreasing run starting at `i` |
| `i` | the current index in each loop |
| `result` | the good indices found, in increasing order |
